 FC Porto prepare for first women's Clássico with five ex-Sporting players 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Fátima Pinto helped Sporting win their first national championship in Porto and is now preparing for another historic first in the same city, this time in blue and white. The first meeting between the Dragons and the Lionesses in women’s football, scheduled for Sunday, brings the Portuguese international’s story together with those of four other current Porto players who previously played for Sporting. For all of them, the Clássico has a history that goes beyond the shirt they now wear.
 Of the five footballers, Fátima Pinto has the longest association with Sporting: 186 appearances, compared with her eight for FC Porto. The match comes as Porto establish themselves in the top flight and pits two projects with different histories against each other, but with several key figures in common.
 OneFootball Videos
 The Madeira-born midfielder’s memories go back to 20 May 2017. That day, she opened the scoring in Sporting’s 6–1 away win over Boavista, a match that secured the Lionesses’ first national title and linked Porto to one of the most important moments of her time at Sporting.
 Fátima Pinto joined Sporting in 2016/17, the season the club returned to senior women’s football. Winning the league and cup double in her first year, a feat repeated the following season, made her one of the faces of a team that quickly found a winning formula.
 Her first departure came in 2022, when she moved to Alavés, before returning to Sporting the following season. Her final farewell came in the summer of 2025, after eight seasons wearing the lion on her chest, followed by a spell at Strasbourg in France.
 In August 2026, FC Porto announced the signing of the Portuguese international for a squad preparing to compete in the national top flight for the first time. The experience she had gained through titles, European competitions and spells abroad was now at the service of a project at a different stage of its development.
 Mariana Azevedo also brings senior experience on both sides to this encounter. The 31-year-old defender made 38 appearances for Sporting and also played for Vilaverdense, FC Famalicão and SC Braga before joining FC Porto last season.
 In the blue-and-white defence, she became a key figure in the campaign that ended with the Second Division title and promotion to Liga BPI. She now has 30 appearances for the Dragons, with her time at the club already featuring a trophy and promotion.
 Ana Teles , 25, has followed another path marked by trophies at Sporting and experience outside Portugal. After playing for SC Braga, the midfielder joined Sporting, where she made 62 appearances and won a Portuguese Cup and a Super Cup.
 Spells at Djurgården in Sweden and Besiktas in Turkey followed, before she returned to Portuguese football to play for Valadares Gaia. She moved to FC Porto last summer and has so far made seven appearances in blue and white.
 For Maria Ferreira, the connection with Sporting began primarily in the youth ranks. Born in Cortiçadas de Lavre, she moved to the Alcochete Academy at the age of 12 and also spent time at Villarreal in Spain before joining FC Porto in 2025.
 When she was unveiled as a Porto signing, the young forward highlighted the club’s approach to promoting women’s football. In an interview published in August 2025, she summed up that impression in one sentence:
 “It’s a club that doesn’t say it wants to do things differently; it does things differently.”
 The move gave her a more prominent role in senior football: after 11 appearances for Sporting’s first team, she now has 40 for FC Porto. At 21, Maria Ferreira’s career also includes a role in the season that brought Porto the Second Division title, linking her own emergence to the team’s growth.
 Sofia Silva completes the group of five current Porto players with a Sporting past. The 24-year-old defender made four appearances for Sporting and also represented SC Braga, Marítimo and Valencia before joining the blue-and-white project.
 With 13 appearances for FC Porto, she was part of the squad that earned promotion to the top flight. Like Mariana Azevedo and Maria Ferreira, she comes into this first Clássico having played a part in the chapter that opened the doors of Liga BPI to Porto.
 There is a sixth career linking the clubs, although the player is no longer in Porto’s current squad. Gabriela Vinhas was on the books at Sporting and FC Porto in 2024/25 and 2025/26 respectively, without making any official first-team appearances; the 21-year-old defender now plays for FC Famalicão.
 Through youth development, trophies and different opportunities in senior football, these connections show how the two projects’ paths crossed before the teams met on the pitch. Sporting have spent a decade in senior women’s football, while FC Porto rose from the Third Division to Liga BPI in just two seasons.
 It is at this meeting of paths that Fátima Pinto could once again have a special role to play. If she takes to the pitch on Sunday, the player who scored in Porto to help Sporting celebrate their first championship will have the chance to take part in another historic first, now wearing the opposition’s shirt.
